note: Source of truth of the feature registry. FEATURE-REGISTRY.md is generated from this file by `cargo xtask features --write` and checked by `cargo xtask features --check` (CI). Never reuse an id. Do not set an implementation status without evidence.

features.name: Voxel coordinates, brick keys and regions
features.description: i64 voxel and brick coordinates, floor division for negative space, cell keys with level, half-open regions.
features.criteria: Negative coordinates symmetric; no overflow wrap; deterministic ordering.

features.name: Sparse brick storage with explicit absent-data states
features.description: Cell store with Present, KnownEmpty, NotLoaded, OutsideBounds and LoadFailure never merged.
features.criteria: Unloaded or failed data is never reported as empty.

features.name: Revisions, epochs and region stamps
features.description: Monotonic per-resource revisions with epochs, incomparable-is-stale rule, region stamps.
features.criteria: Overflow is an error; stamps are order independent.

features.name: Atomic commit gate and mutation boundary
features.description: Single commit primitive reachable only through user, system and recovery handles; batches apply entirely or not at all.
features.criteria: No direct write path; loom model of the gate; compile-fail bypass tests.

features.name: Export/import views and stable content hash
features.description: Plain-data view of an asset and a content fingerprint independent of encoding.
features.criteria: Round trip restores revisions and content; hash independent of channel encoding.

features.name: Geometry bounds
features.description: Checked integer boxes: union, intersection, growth, level conversion, transform; no world-size limit.
features.criteria: Overflow is an error; property tests for the algebra.

features.name: World identity values
features.description: WorldSeed and GeneratorVersion newtypes with fixed-width byte forms.
features.criteria: Exact comparison; stable byte form.

features.name: Material palette (content ids to runtime indices)
features.description: Namespaced content ids, runtime indices with air = 0, collision diagnostics, strict and recovery-mode resolution of saved tables. Provisional (C-10).
features.criteria: Unknown content is an error or a visible placeholder, never another material.

features.name: Mesh-page layers (page store in Core)
features.description: A mesh layer holds mesh pages in the same keyed, revisioned and bounded store as other cells; the commit gate accepts only pages in mesh layers and only channels elsewhere; export/import and the content hash include pages; Processing snapshots accept mesh layers.
features.criteria: Payload mismatch both ways is a typed error; view round trip keeps pages; additive public API only (PageStore::new, cells). Page bytes are opaque to Core.

features.name: Immutable snapshots with apron
features.description: Pin-only brick neighbourhood snapshots with per-brick input stamps.
features.criteria: Snapshot isolation under concurrent commits; apron consistency.

features.name: Derived-data executor with stale-result rejection and caps
features.description: Provider graph, task state machine, cancellation, single publish path that rejects stale results, pin and lifetime budgets.
features.criteria: No stale result is ever published (loom, stress); caps enforced on the synthetic mobile budget.

features.name: Editing API contracts
features.description: Operations, transactions, results, conflicts, authorization context, backend and storage ports.
features.criteria: No behaviour in the crate; API snapshot guards changes.

features.name: Transactional editing through one user commit path
features.description: Authorization, backend dispatch, private overlay, expected-revision conflicts, atomic commit, rollback, cancel.
features.criteria: A failed or conflicting transaction changes nothing; only user commits arise from user requests.

features.name: Idempotent retry by operation id, including after a restart
features.description: Committed operations are not applied twice; the retry table is rebuilt from the journal, bounded safely, and the highest folded sequence per scope is persisted in the manifest so that old retries stay refused after compaction; undecided intents block retries until resolved.
features.criteria: Confirmed op not re-applied after restart or after compaction (several compactions, two actors, bounded table); same id with other content refused; an undecided intent blocks the retry until resolved. Sound under RS-1 (per-scope strictly increasing sequences from the authoritative side); ids that break it are refused. TD-4 itself stays open (resolve_pending caller, CB-1).

features.name: Observers and dirty propagation after commit
features.description: Dirty regions go to Processing, then observers in registration order; observer failures are isolated.
features.criteria: Observers see post-commit state only; order equals commit order. Known limit: callbacks run inside the commit section (TD-1).

features.name: Voxel editing operations
features.description: Set, replace, fill air, clear, copy and move (with rotation) of voxel regions as write sets, at any level, with no world-size limit.
features.criteria: Unloaded bricks never guessed; other channels preserved; brute-force model equality.

features.name: Faces mesh provider (reference oracle)
features.description: Visible unit faces per brick with apron; the correctness reference for meshing.
features.criteria: Equals the brute-force definition across brick borders.

features.name: Greedy mesh provider
features.description: Material-aware greedy merging of coplanar faces; the triangle mesh has no T-junctions (foreign edge vertices are added to merged quads, border planes are never merged). Not the default renderer (GOV-13).
features.criteria: Coverage equals faces; the union of all bricks of random worlds has zero T-junctions on the triangle mesh, across borders and in negative space; pictures from six sides are identical to the faces baseline (software rasteriser); incremental equals full rebuild; deterministic for 1 and 4 workers.

features.name: Incremental mesh rebuild by a dirty rule
features.description: After a commit only the brick and its six face neighbours need new meshes.
features.criteria: Incremental rebuild equals full rebuild over random edits.

features.name: Voxel collision boxes
features.description: Disjoint boxes covering exactly the solid voxels of a brick; unknown is never free space.
features.criteria: Boxes equal the voxel model; stale results never served.

features.name: One-step voxel LOD
features.description: A coarser derived level per brick; presence of thin structures survives.
features.criteria: Equals brute-force coarsening; authoritative data untouched. Mixed-resolution neighbours belong to PS-9.

features.name: SDF backend
features.description: Quantised signed distance field (negative inside, 256 steps per voxel): union, subtraction and material assignment of spheres and boxes as write sets; Surface Nets mesh provider with an apron; gradient normals; collision boxes. No hidden conversion from voxels.
features.criteria: Conformance suite passes; the sphere over eight bricks is one closed, consistently wound manifold without cracks at brick joins (Euler characteristic 2); incremental equals full rebuild; unloaded bricks never guessed; deterministic. Provisional (providers pending O-1, port validate needs a layer: TD-2). CI-host results only.

features.name: Mesh backend
features.description: Authoritative polygon geometry in mesh pages: add a box or triangles, remove, set material; canonical pages, page validator with typed errors, normal recalculation, triangle collision provider. Core stores mesh pages through a page store (additive Core change).
features.criteria: A box over several pages is one closed consistently wound manifold; pages are canonical (history independent); invalid input is a typed refusal and changes nothing; golden collision output. Provisional (collision provider pending O-1). Mesh pages are not clipped at brick borders. CI-host results only.

features.name: Backend conformance suite
features.description: Generic suite every backend must pass, self-checked against broken fakes.
features.criteria: Nine broken fakes are each caught; voxel backend passes.
evidence: tests/sdf_backend.rs and tests/mesh_backend.rs run the generic suite on the SDF and mesh backends

features.name: Versioned checksummed record codec (experimental)
features.description: Asset snapshots, journal records and write batches with schema version, CRC-32 and size limits. Not an approved format.
features.criteria: Every byte flip and truncation detected; hostile counts refused without allocation.

features.name: Atomic snapshot save and load
features.description: Temp file, fsync, rename, directory sync; load verifies the checksum.
features.criteria: Every modelled crash point leaves a complete old or new snapshot. Model and real-directory evidence only; no device durability (DG-2).

features.name: Write-ahead journal with payload and replay
features.description: Intent/Confirmed/Aborted phases, write payload, reconciliation and replay of confirmed changes after the last snapshot.
features.criteria: Replay is idempotent and reproduces the pre-crash world. The journal is a contract fake in tests: no file journal yet; CB-1 (commit and journal not atomic) is open.

features.name: File-backed operation journal
features.description: Append-only checksummed journal file: acknowledged means written and fsynced, gapless sequence, torn tails repaired on open, damage in the middle refused, failures poison the journal.
features.criteria: Every modelled crash point keeps every acknowledged change and replay restores it; a killed child process loses no acknowledged record. A damaged, cut or missing last ACKNOWLEDGED record is never taken for a torn tail: open fails closed (acknowledgement marks); an unacknowledged torn or rotted tail is dropped; mid-log damage, lost or backwards marks and unknown schema are refused. Model, real files and a killed process only: no device durability (DG-2); marks and journal are two files, so loss of the same record in both is undetectable.
evidence: tests/persistence_journal.rs (11 tests incl. negative acknowledged-record tests)

features.name: Manifest, verified snapshot store and crash-safe compaction (experimental)
features.description: One atomically published manifest names a verified snapshot and the journal tail; compaction folds the journal into a new snapshot; opening a world loads the snapshot and journal, refuses damage and removes unnamed leftovers.
features.criteria: Crash at every step of compaction (model, all torn modes) leaves one whole generation and loses no acknowledged record; full cycle on a real directory equals the independent model by content hash; damaged manifest, snapshot or journal refused. Limits: needs exclusive access; retry history before the last compaction is not remembered (L-COMP-1); no device durability (DG-2); format experimental until GOV-10.

features.name: World record (identity, seed, generator version)
features.description: One checksummed record written at creation: world id, seed, generator version, structure version. Opening checks that record and manifest name the same generator, that this build can reproduce it and that the structure version is known; nothing is adapted silently.
features.criteria: Create, generate, edit, kill, load, regenerate the base, replay, equal Core hash, continue editing; creation is crash safe at every step; unknown versions, mismatches and damage are refused. Experimental format until GOV-10; no device durability (DG-2).

features.name: Manifest, snapshot store, world record and compaction
features.description: Manifest with atomic publish, snapshot store with verify step, world record (seed and generator version) and crash-safe compaction keeping the last recoverable state.
features.criteria: PERS-02, PERS-03, PERS-05 and PERS-08 are implemented and crash-tested in the experimental format; PERS-06 (recovery orchestration), PERS-07 (migration) and PERS-09 (composite persistence) are not started; generator version never changed silently.

features.name: Crash-point fault-injection harness
features.description: In-memory filesystem with a weakest-POSIX model and a runner that crashes a scenario after every step.
features.criteria: Finds a missing fsync; a model is not proof of real platform behaviour.

features.name: Final save format
features.description: The approved on-disk format of worlds, journals and snapshots.
features.criteria: GOV-10 approved after RG-1.

features.name: Inventory and creative/survival rules (prototype)
features.description: 27 slots (hotbar 9), stacks of 64, block items from five materials. Survival: mining adds an item (refused when it does not fit), building uses one; creative: every material, nothing consumed. The world change is committed first and the inventory follows; the inventory is saved in game.state next to the world after every change and on quit. Approved scope: owner message of 2026-11-10 ('CUBE PRODUCTION DEVELOPMENT: World Streaming, Building Experience, Inventory and First Gameplay Loop'): unloading of far areas, hotbar, target highlight, placement preview, a first inventory and one small objective. The game rules here are a PROTOTYPE (not a frozen design).
features.criteria: Rust: add, stack, overflow, swap and merge, selection, save text round trip and rejection of damaged files; a full inventory refuses mining and the block stays; the game file survives a restart; a damaged file means a fresh game. Real Godot play smoke: start empty, empty hand refused, 3 mined = 3 items, 12 placed, creative consumes nothing, restart restores the items. The journal and game.state are two stores and cannot be one atomic action, so they are reconciled: game.state records a write-ahead intent (operation sequence and effect) before the world changes, the effect and the cleared intent are written in one flushed file write after the commit, and at the next start an intent still present is settled against the journal (confirmed: the effect is applied once; not confirmed: dropped). Rust tests crash the game at each point between the two writes (4 tests in reconcile.rs, mutation-checked) and a restart settles it; no device crash test (DG-2).
blockers: Rules are PROPOSED (prototype), not an approved design
Inventory is client-side data, not yet validated by an authority (server model)
No crafting, equipment, drops in the world or item entities

features.name: World streaming with unloading around the player (finite world)
features.description: The local host generates bricks around the player on demand and unloads far unedited bricks (a resident budget, hysteresis, the derived cache is dropped with them). A reloaded brick has a higher revision (one per load, never a reset); at open the journal is replayed after each edited brick is brought to the revision its first recorded edit expected, and edited bricks are never unloaded. The world has a finite horizontal edge of 48 bricks. Approved scope: owner message of 2026-11-10 ('CUBE PRODUCTION DEVELOPMENT: World Streaming, Building Experience, Inventory and First Gameplay Loop'): unloading of far areas, hotbar, target highlight, placement preview, a first inventory and one small objective. The game rules here are a PROTOTYPE (not a frozen design).
features.criteria: Rust (6 tests): unload and reload give an identical world and revision +1; an edit after two unload cycles survives a restart with the right revision (fails without the revision step: the edit would be silently lost); edited bricks stay; resident bricks stop growing over a 40-brick walk there and back and the world at the start equals a fresh one; concurrent requests generate each brick once; a session keeps residency and the derived cache bounded. Real Godot 4.2.2 journey smoke: 150 voxels out and back, 1458 bricks unloaded, resident 1331 -> about 1100 and flat on the way back, derived cache <= 560 entries, process working set 169-178 MB (debug build, 12 samples), 8-10 ms per frame while generating and unloading (debug build, vsync off, RTX 3070 Ti). Not in CI.
blockers: Edited bricks are never unloaded: a player who builds over a huge area keeps all of it resident (unloading edited bricks needs a snapshot or per-brick reload path)
Generation runs on the main thread (budgeted 48 bricks per frame; not measured under heavier worlds)
Journey measured over 150 voxels in the real game and 640 in Rust, not a long soak
WGEN-02..04 (service, materialiser design) still gated

features.name: Visual QA of Godot screenshots with TypeSafe Jev (experimental tool)
features.description: A standard-library Python tool (tools/visual-qa) that sends a Godot screenshot, or a before and after pair, with typed questions (Noul, Choice, gated Box) to TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and produces a PASS, WARN, FAIL or UNKNOWN report in JSON and Markdown. Dry run by default; a live call needs an explicit flag and TYPESAFE_API_KEY. TypeSafe takes no part in generation, rendering or the game loop; geometry invariants stay in the Rust tests. Approved scope: owner message of 2026-11-10 (Visual QA integration).
features.criteria: Experimental, advisory only. v2 measured (calibration 9 answered, evaluation 14 answered, run once, questionnaires frozen by hash): TypeSafe terrain-integrity found missing or hidden geometry and a wrong material (evaluation 6 of 6, no false positive at the fixed 0.7/0.3 thresholds, but about half of the good pictures sit in the unsure band); scene-smoke and block-edit showed no value beyond code (the 2 real one-block edits were missed); Box IoU 0.23 to 0.95, not for production. Deterministic checks found 4 of 4 partial loads and 5 of 5 stale updates with no false alarms. 25 requests in the v2 stage (22 answered, 3 HTTP 529 not retried), about 80k input tokens, about $0.003. Small samples: counts, not rates. v3 (offline + real Godot, no live request): a one-command suite generates reproducible scenarios (camera, world, editing, occlusion), executes them in the real Godot scene (20 of 20 executed, identical statuses and metrics on a second run), checks them deterministically (pose, bricks, edits, restore and persistence by picture), and plans batched visual-only TypeSafe questions under the documented limits (SINGLE/BATCH/ADAPTIVE, spend ledger, dry run by default). Collision and penetration tests are not possible (no API). v3 live (8 requests, no errors, about $0.0015): on 7 pictures the merged request matched all 7 labels and one request per picture matched 6 (1 unsure); the new occlusion question agreed with 4 of 4 injected overlays and the healthy control (exploratory, uncalibrated). Not in CI, not required, not player-visible. External dependency: TypeSafe API (image support in preview).
evidence: labels committed before any v2 request: 8988b36
blockers: Evaluation set is used up: any rework of the questions needs a new calibration set
Thin evidence: 15 defective pictures, 2 real edit pairs, no real-renderer bugs
TypeSafe image support is experimental
v3 live evidence is 7 pictures with large injected faults, no calibration split; batching effect on accuracy unproven (one pair of runs)
